subject: MSA + Order Form: carve-outs for OSS/model license liability and caps
messages:

Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: carve-outs for OSS/model license liability and caps

Hi Camila —

Thanks for sending the latest MSA and order form. A few items jumped out from our side on the liability section and model licensing:

- We need clarity on how Redwood will treat open-source components and third-party model weights when it comes to IP infringement and indemnity.
- Our procurement policy requires either (a) a pass-through indemnity where Redwood will enforce claims against upstream licensors, or (b) an explicit cap carve-out for OSS-related IP claims.
- Consequential damages carve-outs: we prefer that our customer compensatory remedies for downstream losses (e.g., regulatory fines, customer remediation) be excluded from a strict liability cap in the event of proven IP infringement arising from an OSS component.

Can you share Redwood’s proposed language and whether the Order Form can list model-provider license obligations separately? Also please attach your redlines.

Best,
Nora
Nora Patel
VP Legal Operations, NovaFin

Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: carve-outs for OSS/model license liability and caps

Nora —

Appreciate the clear ask. Looping in our legal lead Lauren and Marcus from solutions/infra so we can give a consolidated response and a redline.

Quick answers up front:
- We do not generally agree to uncapped pass-through indemnities for upstream licensor claims, but we can offer specific carve-outs and a limited OSS indemnity tied to direct damage and to the extent the alleged infringement is traceable to Redwood-controlled code or distribution.
- We can add an appendix to the Order Form that lists model providers and their license constraints; that appendix will be non-exhaustive and updated as models change.
- Consequential damages: our standard MSA waives consequential and special damages, but we can negotiate specific exceptions for direct regulatory fines resulting from proven IP infringement in the OSS components if we accept a higher monetary cap.

Attaching our current marked-up MSA + Order Form and a license inventory extract for the models proposed. Lauren: can you propose precise redline language for the MSA cap and the OSS indemnity? Marcus: can you confirm whether we can provide a per-model license appendix that is programmatically exported from your inventory?

Thanks — I’ll hold on next steps until we have legal’s wording.

—
Camila Reyes

From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: camila_reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Nora Patel <nora.patel@novafin.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 11:30:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: MSA + Order Form: carve-outs for OSS/model license liability and caps

Nora/Camila —

Thanks for the summary, Camila. Below is proposed redline text and negotiating positions from legal. I’ve kept the language targeted so we avoid broad pass-through exposure while offering NovaFin reasonable protection.

1) OSS / Third-Party Model License Indemnity (proposed MSA section):
"Redwood will indemnify, defend and hold Customer harmless from and against any final judgment awarded against Customer for direct monetary damages to the extent arising from a third party claim that the Redwood-delivered software or model weights, as distributed by Redwood under this Agreement, infringe a third party's patents, copyrights, or trademarks, provided that: (a) Customer notifies Redwood promptly in writing of the claim; (b) Redwood has sole control of the defense and settlement of the claim; and (c) Customer reasonably cooperates with Redwood's defense. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood's indemnity obligations shall not extend to (i) any third-party components or model weights provided directly by Customer or by a third party under Customer's separate license; or (ii) open source software used by Customer independent of Redwood's distribution."
Negotiating note: we propose limiting scope to infringement that is traceable to Redwood's distribution and code paths so we are not liable for customer-supplied models or for independent OSS use.

2) Monetary Cap and OSS carve-outs (proposed MSA section):
"Except for Redwood's indemnity obligations for IP infringement as set forth above and except for Customer's claims for Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct, Redwood's liability under this Agreement shall be limited to the greater of (a) the total fees paid by Customer to Redwood under the Order Form giving rise to the claim in the twelve (12) months prior to the claim, or (b) USD 2,000,000. For claims solely arising from Redwood's breach of its obligations under the OSS Indemnity provision, the cap shall be increased to the greater of (i) the fees paid in the twelve (12) months prior to the claim and (ii) USD 3,000,000."
Negotiating note: we can flex the numbers (2M / 3M) if needed, but we need to keep a hard upper bound. We will not accept an uncapped pass-through indemnity.

3) Consequential damages / regulatory fines carve-out:
"Neither party shall be liable for indirect, special, incidental, consequential, or punitive damages, including loss of profits, loss of business, or loss of data, except that the foregoing exclusion shall not apply to (a) damages awarded for a party's gross negligence or willful misconduct, and (b) direct regulatory fines and penalties finally assessed against Customer solely to the extent caused by Redwood's willful breach of its obligations under the OSS Indemnity provision, subject to the monetary cap set forth above."
Rationale: this gives NovaFin protection for narrowly-defined regulatory fines tied to Redwood-originated OSS infringement while preserving our overall cap structure.

4) Order Form appendix: Marcus, we should provide an appendix listing model providers and a short license note (e.g., "Model X: Apache 2.0; Model Y: non-commercial license — restricted weights"). Recommend we make the appendix "informational" and not a warranty; any license breach claims must be routed through the OSS Indemnity above.

Please confirm whether these positions are acceptable as our opening legal stance. If NovaFin needs a higher cap for OSS claims, we can consider USD 5,000,000 at senior approval.

—
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0162

From: OutsideCounsel (Novafin Legal) <legal@novafin-legal.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, camila_reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Nora Patel <nora.patel@novafin.com>, Edward Chu <edward.chu@novafin.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 13:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: carve-outs for OSS/model license liability and caps

Lauren/Camila —

Thanks for the proposed text. A few counterpoints from NovaFin:

- NovaFin cannot accept language that ties indemnity only to "traceable to Redwood distribution" without an explicit mechanism that allows Redwood to pursue an upstream claim or to require remediation from the model provider. We will consider a limited pass-through where Redwood is obligated to pursue remedies against upstream licensors if the claim relates to their licensed model weights.
- Regarding caps: we can accept a 3M cap for OSS-related indemnity, but not a 2M general cap if our annual committed spend under the Order Form exceeds that amount. We propose: general cap = greater of fees in prior 12 months or USD 5,000,000; OSS-specific cap = greater of fees in prior 12 months or USD 7,500,000.
- Consequential damages: we need an explicit carve-out for regulatory fines and mandatory customer remediation costs where such damages are the direct result of an IP infringement attributable to an OSS component distributed by Redwood. That should be outside the liability cap for OSS claims only.

Additionally, please provide (a) evidence of SOC 2 that covers model deployment controls and (b) the full license inventory for all models referenced in the order form (not just a partial extract).

If Redwood is open to a negotiation path: we suggest Redwood accept the 3M OSS cap fence with a contractual obligation to use commercially reasonable efforts to enforce upstream licensor obligations (and provide NovaFin with remediation status updates).

Regards,
Outside Counsel (for NovaFin)
legal@novafin-legal.com
+1 212-555-0200

From: camila_reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 16:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: carve-outs for OSS/model license liability and caps

Nora / Team —

Thanks for the thoughtful response and proposed numbers. Quick summary / next steps so we stay aligned:

1) Redwood position: we will not accept an uncapped pass-through indemnity. However, we can agree to: (a) an OSS indemnity that covers direct infringement claims tied to Redwood-distributed code and weights, (b) an obligation to use commercially reasonable efforts to pursue upstream remediation or enforcement where a covered claim implicates a model provider, and (c) periodic remediation status updates to NovaFin.

2) Caps: Redwood legal is prepared to escalate to approve higher caps. Current internal fallback ranges: General cap up to USD 5,000,000 and OSS-specific cap up to USD 7,500,000 with VP-level sign-off. Lauren, please flag if you see regulatory/commercial risk at those levels.

3) Consequential/regulatory fines: we can carve out regulatory fines tied to proven Redwood-originated OSS infringement, but only to the extent limited by the OSS-specific cap. We cannot agree to make such fines entirely unlimited.

4) Deliverables: Marcus will export a complete license inventory for all models listed in the Order Form; Lauren will produce a clean redline with the proposed language above plus a short appendix template for the model-license listing. I will coordinate an internal escalation if NovaFin wants the 7.5M OSS cap.

5) Timeline: plan to have an internal legal approval decision and updated DocuSign-ready redline by end of week (EOW Fri 20 Feb). If you need faster, let me know and I’ll push.

Attaching the updated Order Form v3 with the model appendix stub.

Thanks —
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
